title: Anthropic Reveals How Scientists Really Use Claude for Research
dek: Data analysis and writing dominate, while AI ideation lags far behind.

facts.label: Claude Code sessions on data analysis

caption:
Scientists say ideas matter most. So why do they barely use AI for them? 🔬

Anthropic studied 207,049 research sessions on Claude and Claude Code. Data analysis and writing dominate, while idea generation gets just 4.2% of Claude sessions. Computer science is only 4.3% of the world's researchers but drives 32.7% of Claude Code research sessions.

The report also models how much faster science could move. If AI handled all non-physical research work, computer science and statistics could see up to a 15-fold increase in output, while lab-bound fields like chemistry and biology would rise about three- or fourfold.

We break down the full study on AI Parabellum. Would you trust AI to come up with your next hypothesis?

post_caption:
Where does AI actually help researchers? Anthropic's new data says crunching numbers and drafting papers, not dreaming up hypotheses.

Specialized Claude Science runs over 70% of sessions with high AI autonomy, and about 40% of surveyed researchers expect AI to run full projects on its own by 2030. 📊
